newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Pharmavene gives Shire U.S. foothold.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Pharmavene gives Shire U.S. foothold.

text.p: Drugs development company Shire Pharmaceuticals Group Plc on Tuesday said it wants to acquire Pharmavene Inc from the U.S. for an initial 55.5 million pounds ($90.5 million).
The deal would increase Shire's size by more than a third and give the British company a foothold outside its homebase.
Pharmavene -- which is based in Rockville, Maryland -- works on so-called "delivery technologies" which improve the absorbtion of existing medicines.
The Pharmavene buy would help make Shire's drugs become more attractive and give the British company experience in dealing with the U.S. Food and Drugs Administration (FDA).
The FDA is the authority which decides whether a product can be marketed in the U.S.
Shire, which has a market capitalisation of about 142 million pounds, makes drugs to treat bone diseases, such as osteoporis, and also Alzheimer's disease.
The Pharmavene purchase would be Shire's first major move in its 11-year existence to gain more market clout.
"We had to break out of Europe sooner or later. We have perhaps done it rather sooner than we originally envisaged, but that's all for the good," said finance director Stephen Stamp.
Pharmavene posted a net loss of $4.7 million on turnover of $4.5 million in 1996.
Stamp said Shire's next step would be aimed at boosting its marketing presence outside Britain; likely through purchases in continental Europe and eventually the U.S. again.
"It is unlikely we will start with one man and one car. It is more likely to come through an acquisition, but there is no rush," Stamp told Reuters.
Shire wants to become less dependent on marketing partners and reap the full awards from the drugs it has developed by selling them itself.
Shire is to satisfy Pharmavene's acquisition by paying 15.3 million pounds in cash and 40.2 million pounds in new shares.
On top of the initial consideration of 55.5 million pounds, Shire will pay up to 6.1 million pounds in cash upon receipt of a milestone payment from a licensee of Pharmavene.

The drug development company said it will also make further deferred contingent payments capped at 42.9 million pounds and plans to raise 11.5 million through a placing of new shares at 214 pence per share.
Together with the Pharmavene acquistion, Shire reported a first-half pretax loss of 0.1 million pounds, down from a 4.6 million profit a year earlier.
The results were hit by licencing arrangements with Johnson & Johnson unit Janssen for Shire's Galantamine drug, Shire said.
"Excluding the exceptional nature of these arrangements, the group's underlying trading position improved significantly in the half year under review," it added.
Shire shares fell 3-1/2 pence to 234 pence at midsession.
